```{r}
rm(list = ls())
```

## ============================================================
## Strategy: train on 2015–2022 (8 years), test on 2023–2024 (2 years)
### Apply to all 4 districts consistently
## ============================================================

```{r}
library(ftsa)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
```

## ----------------------------------------------------------
## Helper: compute accuracy metrics for one district
## ----------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
forecast_district <- function(csv_file, district_name,
                              forecast_horizon = 6,
                              order = 3) {
  
  # Read data
  df <- read.csv(csv_file)
  y_mat <- as.matrix(df)
  
  # Set column names as years
  n_years <- ncol(y_mat)
  years <- 2015:(2014 + n_years)
  colnames(y_mat) <- as.character(years)
  
  # Use all available data for training
  y_train <- y_mat  # Use all columns
  
  # Months (1-12)
  x <- 1:nrow(y_mat)
  
  # Create functional time series object
  fts_train <- fts(x = x,
                   y = y_train,
                   xname = "Month",
                   yname = "Water Table Depth")
  
  # Fit functional time series model
  fit <- ftsm(fts_train, order = order, method = "rapca")
  
  # Forecast for specified horizon
  fc <- forecast(fit, h = forecast_horizon, method = "arfima")
  
  # Extract forecasted values
  y_forecast <- fc$mean$y  # 12 x forecast_horizon matrix
  
  # Get forecast years
  forecast_years <- (max(years) + 1):(max(years) + forecast_horizon)
  colnames(y_forecast) <- as.character(forecast_years)
  
  # Extract variance explained by each functional principal component
  varprop <- fit$varprop
  
  # Return results
  list(
    district = district_name,
    years = years,
    forecast_years = forecast_years,
    y_train = y_train,
    y_forecast = y_forecast,
    x = x,
    varprop = varprop,
    fit = fit,
    forecast_object = fc
  )
}
```

## ----------------------------------------------------------
## Run for all 4 districts
### Adjust file paths to match your working directory
## ----------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
results <- list(
  forecast_district("Borguna.csv", "Barguna", order = 3),
  forecast_district("Joypurhat.csv", "Joypurhat", order = 3),
  forecast_district("Mymensingh.csv", "Mymensingh", order = 3),
  forecast_district("Netrokona.csv", "Netrokona", order = 5)
)
```

#### Note: Netrokona uses order=5 due to its lower PC1 variance explained (37.8%)

## ----------------------------------------------------------
## Display model diagnostics
## ----------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
cat("\n=== Model Diagnostics ===\n")
for (r in results) {
  cat("\n", r$district, ":\n", sep = "")
  cat("  Functional Principal Components Variance Explained:\n")
  for (i in 1:length(r$varprop)) {
    cat(sprintf("    PC%d: %.1f%%\n", i, r$varprop[i] * 100))
  }
  cat(sprintf("  Total variance explained by top %d PCs: %.1f%%\n", 
              length(r$varprop), sum(r$varprop) * 100))
}
```

```{r,fig.width=15,fig.height=10}
# Set up plotting parameters
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))

for (r in results) {
  # Plot training data (all historical years)
  matplot(r$x, r$y_train,
          type = "l", 
          col = colorRampPalette(c("grey70", "grey40"))(ncol(r$y_train)),
          lty = 1, 
          lwd = 1.5,
          xlab = "Month", 
          ylab = "Water Table Depth (m)",
          main = r$district,
          xaxt = "n",
          ylim = range(c(r$y_train, r$y_forecast), na.rm = TRUE))
  
  # Add month labels
  axis(1, at = 1:12, labels = month.abb, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7)
  
  # Add forecasted years with distinct colors
  n_forecast <- ncol(r$y_forecast)
  forecast_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("red","orange","blue"))(n_forecast)
  
  matlines(r$x, r$y_forecast, 
           col = forecast_colors, 
           lty = 2, 
           lwd = 2)
  
  # Add legend
  legend("topright",
         legend = c(paste(r$forecast_years)),
         col = c(forecast_colors),
         lty = c(rep(2, n_forecast)),
         lwd = c(rep(2, n_forecast)),
         cex = 0.5, 
         bty = "n",
         ncol = 2)
  
  # Add model information
  mtext(sprintf("Model order = %d | Total var explained = %.1f%%", 
                length(r$varprop), sum(r$varprop) * 100),
        side = 3, line = -1.5, cex = 0.6, col = "grey30")
}

# Add overall title
mtext("Groundwater Level Forecasts (2025-2030)", 
      outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2, font = 2)
```
